findings.description: The separator condition was inverted to `not any_prefix_is_slash`, so the separator choice is backwards: options with slash prefixes get "; " and ordinary options get " / ".
findings.rationale: The original code used `"; " if any_prefix_is_slash else " / "`. For a normal option such as `--verbose` with `-v`, any_prefix_is_slash is False, so the new expression yields "; ", producing help text like `-v; --verbose` where it previously showed `-v, --verbose`-style output with " / ". This changes the rendered help for every option with multiple spellings, and the help left column becomes wrong for the common case.
